column2: The narrative transition after Moses' death introduces Joshua son of Nun as Moses' attendant, retaining the service distinction before the divine speech.
Moses' death, now therefore, rising and crossing with all the people remain; the land is given them, not silently changed to you.
Every place trodden by the people's feet is promised, preserving the plural addressees and the earlier word to Moses.
The selected boundaries include Anti-Lebanon, the great Euphrates and the furthest western sea; no absent Hittite-land phrase is added.
The initial you is plural, while your life and the subsequent assurances address Joshua singularly; forsaking and disregarding remain separate negatives.
Joshua apportions the promised land to the people; your fathers is plural amid singular address to him.
Strength and courage concern keeping and doing Moses' commands, with neither right nor left departure and understanding in all conduct retained.
Mouth, day-and-night meditation, understanding-to-do, two prosperity expressions and the final understanding remain; the repetition is not reduced to a slogan.
Behold and the completed command precede strength and courage, two fear prohibitions and the assurance of divine presence everywhere he goes.
Joshua commands the people's scribes, retaining grammateis rather than silently identifying them with every previously named officer class.
Provisions are prepared for crossing this Jordan in three days, with the Lord identified as the God of their fathers.
Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh are singled out as the eastern-allotment recipients.
The Lord has already given rest and this land in the quoted reminder, preserving the selected past forms.
Wives, children and livestock remain while every strong man crosses equipped before his brothers and fights alongside them.
column3: The unexpressed giver's referent is left in the inherited he; the immediate divine giver and Moses' distributive role in 1:15 warrant a later referent check before capitalization is changed.

column2: Your God shifts to our God, and each returns to his own eastern inheritance after the brothers receive rest and land.
The reply promises all commanded actions and travel to every place Joshua sends them.
The people compare obedience to Moses with obedience to Joshua, asking that our God be with him; only represents plen here.
Propose and for or between disobedience and non-hearing, preserving the selected coordinating kai. Replace final Only with But for alla, which does not restrict the exhortation to strength alone.
Two young men leave Shittim, inspect land and Jericho, and lodge with Rahab the harlot; neither the number nor her stated occupation is removed.
The king receives a report of Israelite men entering to spy on the land, preserving the reported information rather than adding their names.
The king's message identifies their night entry into Rahab's house and demands their production because of espionage.
Rahab hides the men and addresses the messengers; messengers is a contextual identification of the otherwise pronominal recipients, not an additional named group.
Her account has departure at the dark gate-closing, ignorance of destination and a conditional prospect of overtaking them.
The retrospective hiding on the roof among flax stalks contrasts with her report of departure, with her agency in piling the stalks retained.
Pursuit runs toward the Jordan crossings, the gate closes, and the final temporal clause continues into 2:8 as in the selected arrangement.
The young men have not yet slept when Rahab goes up to them; young men clarifies the pronominal subject from the narrative.
Rahab knows the land is given and that fear has fallen upon her people; no absent universal-melting clause is supplied here.
The Lord God dried the Red Sea and acted against Sihon and Og, while you destroyed them preserves the change of agent.
Astonished hearts and absence of spirit express fear; the confession names God in heaven above and earth below.
The oath by the Lord God asks reciprocal mercy for her father's house in response to her present mercy.
Propose all that belongs to them for all who belong to them: the selected neuter all that they have is broader than persons alone. The repeated household groups and rescue of my life remain.
The spies' life pledge uses plural yours; Rahab then resumes speaking, asking mercy and faithfulness when the city is delivered.
The selected short verse has lowering through the window, without importing a rope or a house-on-wall explanation.
The hill-country hiding lasts three days until the pursuers return, after which the spies continue on their way.
The oath declaration retains present we are free and singular your to Rahab.
column3: The declaration's relationship to the conditions in 2:18-20 remains syntactically difficult; no unexpressed unless clause is silently inserted into this unit.

column2: Part of the city is retained; the scarlet cord marks the lowering window and the fourfold family gathering stays explicit.
column3: The force of entering part of the city remains open and is not harmonized to a different invasion formulation.

column2: Those leaving the door bear their own guilt; the spies accept responsibility for those remaining with Rahab inside, retaining both oath-liability conditions.
Anyone, not Rahab alone, can wrong the spies or reveal their words and release them from the oath.
Rahab agrees to their word and sends them away; no unexpressed immediate tying of the cord is added here.
The three-day hiding and unsuccessful search of all roads fulfil the earlier plan.
Both young men descend, cross to Joshua son of Nun and report everything that happened.
The land is delivered into our hand and every inhabitant cowers before us, preserving the collective singular hand and comprehensive report.
Joshua rises early; the group departs Shittim and lodges by Jordan before crossing, retaining the change from singular to plural actors.
The scribes pass through camp after three days, preserving the interval without collapsing it into 1:11's speech.
Our God, our priests and the Levites precede the command to leave places and follow the ark; the priest/Levite coordination remains.
About two thousand cubits separates people and ark; keeping distance permits knowing the unfamiliar way, with before rendering the yesterday/third-day idiom.
Purification is for tomorrow and tomorrow is repeated before the promised wonders among the people.
The full ark-of-the-covenant-of-the-Lord title occurs in both command and fulfilment, with the priests ahead of the people.
The Lord begins exalting Joshua today so Israel recognizes the Moses/Joshua parallel of divine presence.
The priests enter the water's edge and stand in Jordan; the inherited idiomatic waters does not imply a different body of water.
Joshua summons Israel to hear the singular word of the Lord our God, preserving the inclusive possessive.
The living God is among you and destroys before us; all seven peoples remain in the selected Canaanite-to-Jebusite order.
The ark belongs to the covenant of the Lord of all the earth, with the full title and present crossing retained.
Twelve men are selected, exactly one from each tribe, without naming them in advance.
When the ark-bearers' feet rest in Jordan's water, the river's water fails and the descending water stands; the two water clauses remain distinct.
The people leave their tents and the priests lift the ark ahead of them, preserving the successive subjects.
The repeated ark titles, immersed priestly feet, full bank and comparison with wheat-harvest days remain in the long temporal clause.
column3: As in the days preserves hosei; whether this comparison specifies the present season or describes a comparable fullness remains open.

column2: The doubled intensifier remains very, very far; Kiriath-jearim, Arabah/Salt Sea and the people's position opposite Jericho retain the selected geography.
Priests stand on dry ground while all Israel crosses on dry ground until the whole people finishes; the repetitions are retained.
